summary: The implementation correctly adds `startswith` and `endswith` methods to Query class. They match only string values (non-strings like None, numbers, missing fields, lists don't match and don't error), are case-sensitive, and work with nested paths. Caching works correctly (same query objects are equal and have same hash). All 264 tests pass including the 6 new tests.

checks.claim: startswith/endswith match only strings and ignore non-strings
checks.evidence: python -c test shows missing field, None, number, list fields don't match; only 'Alice', 'Alan', 'Al', 'ALICE' match startswith('A')

checks.claim: Caching works correctly for new query methods
checks.evidence: python -c test shows q1 == q2 and hash(q1) == hash(q2) for identical startswith queries; different prefixes produce different hashes

checks.claim: All tests pass including new tests
checks.evidence: python -m pytest -v shows 264 passed including 6 new tests in test_startswith_seed.py

findings.text: Empty string prefix/suffix matches all strings (including empty string) - this is standard Python behavior but worth noting
